name: leaf_exponent_mono
code:
/-- P0082 page 371, scalar auxiliary for merging two ranges of orders. The cancellation input remains cited.
Exact clean companion for an elementary open leaf. -/
theorem leaf_exponent_mono (cA c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hcA : c ≤ cA) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - cA / (k : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - c / (k : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  apply Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by exact_mod_cast hN)
  have hdiv := div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hcA (sq_nonneg (k : ℝ))
  linarith
twin: For a natural base N at least one, reducing the positive gain c in the exponent one minus c over k squared increases the real power.
instance: Take N one, k one and c equal to cA equal to one. Both powers are one.
source: P0082 page 371, scalar auxiliary for merging two ranges of orders. The cancellation input remains cited.

name: leaf_odd_upper_window_split
code:
/-- P0082 page 367 display 30, finite interval bookkeeping auxiliary. These midpoint choices belong to the formal split.
Exact clean companion for an elementary open leaf. -/
theorem leaf_odd_upper_window_split (N : ℕ) (hN : 100 ≤ N) :
    Finset.Icc ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1) N =
      Finset.Icc ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)
          (((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1) + (N - ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)) / 2) ∪
        Finset.Icc (((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1) + (N - ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)) / 2 + 1) N := by
  ext n
  simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_union]
  omega
twin: For N at least one hundred, the artificial upper odd moment window is the union of its two consecutive halves.
instance: At N one hundred the window from 76 to 100 is the union of the intervals from 76 to 88 and from 89 to 100.
source: P0082 page 367 display 30, finite interval bookkeeping auxiliary. These midpoint choices belong to the formal split.

name: leaf_odd_upper_window_disjoint
code:
/-- P0082 page 367 display 30, finite interval bookkeeping auxiliary.
Exact clean companion for an elementary open leaf. -/
theorem leaf_odd_upper_window_disjoint (γ : ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    Disjoint
      ((Finset.Icc ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)
          (((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1) + (N - ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)) / 2)).filter
        (fun n : ℕ => Odd (nu γ n)))
      ((Finset.Icc (((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1) + (N - ((N + 1) / 2 + N / 4 + 1)) / 2 + 1) N).filter
        (fun n : ℕ => Odd (nu γ n))) := by
  apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
  intro n hn hn'
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hn hn'
  omega
twin: The odd index filters of the two consecutive halves are disjoint for every N and gamma.
instance: At N one hundred the two unfiltered halves are nonempty and disjoint. The assertion holds for gamma 5/4.
source: P0082 page 367 display 30, finite interval bookkeeping auxiliary.

name: leaf_odd_moment_add_const
code:
/-- P0082 page 367 display 30, scalar auxiliary for adding two window bounds.
Exact clean companion for an elementary open leaf. -/
theorem leaf_odd_moment_add_const (M x y A B : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (hx : x ≤ A * M) (hy : y ≤ B * M) : x + y ≤ (A + B + 1) * M := by
  nlinarith
twin: If x is at most A times M and y is at most B times M, with M nonnegative, their sum is at most A plus B plus one times M.
instance: Take M one, x one, y one and A and B both one. The conclusion is two at most three.
source: P0082 page 367 display 30, scalar auxiliary for adding two window bounds.
